answer: One workable design: score identities on graph independence, not headcount, because reef only stays cheap while a clique of fresh wallets answers only each other and its independence score collapses. Concretely, nectar is enforced in the ledger: Detection is retrospective: payouts for a flagged cluster are clawed back after the fact. Any bridge approach that skips this just moves the cost from the attacker to honest miners, which is worse. That converts sybil attacks from an economic play into a pure loss.
